Part 1 Project: Fix-It Tables for the Alder Row Repair Café

The project that closes Part 1 (Sessions 1 to 9): Fix-It Tables, a small phone app for a NEW fictional client, the Alder Row Repair Café, a neighborhood repair café where volunteer fixers sit at four tables and neighbors bring broken things. Contact: Rosa Delgado-Finch, the café's volunteer coordinator. The app is today's repair queue: tickets searchable by item or name, finished repairs hidden on request, grouped by table, readable in dark mode, one press to mark a repair done. Typed screens, components, layout, touch and input and a themed list, from LOCAL typed data (no API). Alone or in pairs.

Covers Modules 1–3Kickoff Session 8Check-in Session 9Due 1 week after Session 9Rubric 12 points, complete = no row at 0

Part 1 Project: The Brief (as the Instructor Sees It)

Files. labs/projects/part1-alder-row-repair-cafe/: TASKS.md (the brief: client, what is given, TODO A to D, how to run it, done-when, milestones, rubric, stretch, journal), RUBRIC.md, lab.json, starter/ (handed out) and solution/ (the model and INSTRUCTOR-NOTES.md; never handed out before scoring). Part 1 Project: Scoring Guidance by Row

  1. Types and data. npm run typecheck: nothing after the two > lines (the type tests in src/types.check.ts pass only with exact unions). Open types.ts: unions, fixer?: string, number: number; no any, no as in src/ outside the starter's leftovers. Strong = comments on the words; adding 'collected' makes tsc list statusLabels and statusTones (the written part's W3).
  2. Components and layout. TicketCard and the screen separate, typed props; the given parts imported, not copied. The card's top row a flexbox row with the name allowed to wrap. Strong = spacing tokens, no stray numbers.
  3. Touch and input. Tests C3, C4, D2 and D4 pass. Read the header: an element. Labels on the switches and the toggles; accessibilityState={{ expanded }}; markFixed builds a new array. Strong = 48-point targets, and the learner explains the copy.
  4. The themed list. Tests D1, D3 and D5 pass. A FlatList with {...screen}, keyExtractor from the id, key={columns}; the web preview at 1024 wide (two columns, no error) and in dark mode (no hard-coded colors). The grouped SectionList's headings have a background.
  5. Accessibility and the phone. npm run lint: 0 problems. A screen-reader or keyboard pass in the web preview: a card's heading, its status, the toggle's name and state. Strong = written down, plus a look on a phone if they have one.

Part 1 Project: Model Solution

The model meets every row and reaches "strong" on rows 1, 3 and 4; the stretch items are left to learners. src/types.ts:

// What the repair café sorts its tickets by: the four repair tables
export type Category = 'electronics' | 'textiles' | 'bikes' | 'furniture';

// Where a ticket is today: waiting for a fixer, on a table, done, or given back unrepaired
export type TicketStatus = 'waiting' | 'in-repair' | 'fixed' | 'not-fixable';

// One item a neighbor brought in
export type Ticket = {
  id: string;
  number: number; // the number on the paper tag tied to the item
  item: string;
  category: Category;
  owner: string; // first name only
  status: TicketStatus;
  fixer?: string; // only once a fixer has picked it up
  problem: string;
};

src/utils/tickets.ts, the rules (the label tables above them are Records):

// Finished = it went home today, repaired or not
export function isFinished(status: TicketStatus): boolean {
  return status === 'fixed' || status === 'not-fixable';
}

// The item or the owner's name contains the search, ignoring case and spaces around it
export function matchesSearch(ticket: Ticket, query: string): boolean {
  const q = query.trim().toLowerCase();
  return q === '' || ticket.item.toLowerCase().includes(q) || ticket.owner.toLowerCase().includes(q);
}

// The tickets the screen shows: worked out on every render, never stored
export function filterTickets(tickets: Ticket[], query: string, hideFinished: boolean): Ticket[] {
  return tickets.filter((ticket) => matchesSearch(ticket, query) && !(hideFinished && isFinished(ticket.status)));
}

// "12 tickets" when all show, "3 of 12 tickets" while filtering
export function countLabel(shown: number, total: number): string {
  return shown === total ? `${total} tickets` : `${shown} of ${total} tickets`;
}

// One table and its tickets: the shape SectionList wants
export type TableSection = { title: string; data: Ticket[] };

// The tickets under their tables, in hall order, leaving out tables with nothing on them
export function groupByCategory(tickets: Ticket[]): TableSection[] {
  return categories
    .map((category) => ({ title: categoryLabels[category], data: tickets.filter((t) => t.category === category) }))
    .filter((section) => section.data.length > 0);
}

src/app/index.tsx, the state and the derived list (the header, the two lists and the styles follow it in solution/):

export default function Queue() {
  const [tickets, setTickets] = useState<Ticket[]>(todaysTickets);
  const [query, setQuery] = useState('');
  const [hideFinished, setHideFinished] = useState(false);
  const [grouped, setGrouped] = useState(false);
  const screen = useScreenScroll();
  const columns = useColumns();
  const styles = useStyles();

  // Derived on every render from the state above: never stored
  const shown = filterTickets(tickets, query, hideFinished);

  // A fixer finished a repair: a NEW array with a NEW ticket in it, so React sees the change
  function markFixed(id: string) {
    setTickets((current) => current.map((t): Ticket => (t.id === id ? { ...t, status: 'fixed' } : t)));
  }

  function showAll() {
    setQuery('');
    setHideFinished(false);
  }
  // ... the header element, the empty state, the SectionList or the FlatList (see solution/)
}

Part 1 Project: Instructor Notes

  • Sizing. The kickoff (50 minutes in Session 8) gets everyone through setup and TODO A, and most into TODO B. The rest is three to four hours at home before the Session 9 check-in, plus polish before the hand-in a week later. TODO D is Lesson 3.1's Cleanups screen with other names: learners who finished that lesson project have every pattern they need.
  • Why local data. Part 1 ends before the app talks to a server over a phone's network (Module 5). Everything runs from src/data/tickets.ts: no API, no network, no account. Learners who know fetch already may not add it: the rubric scores what Part 1 teaches.
  • Where it lives. In the learner's course folder, at shoreline/labs/projects/part1-alder-row-repair-cafe/: they work in starter/ (or in a copy of it called mine/ next to it: any folder three levels under labs/ finds the labs' one shared install, so there is nothing to install). Never inside shoreline-crew. npm run web in it while Shoreline Crew's Metro runs: Expo offers the next port (answer yes).
  • No phone needed. The tests (Jest with React Native's renderer), the type check, the linter and the web preview (npm run web, w) cover every row. A learner with Expo Go can scan the code and see it on a phone; the rubric's "strong" for row 5 asks for a look on a phone only if they have one.
  • The type tests (TODO A). While Category or TicketStatus is still string, tsc reports TS2578 Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive in src/types.check.ts, and the data file reports the fields Ticket does not have yet (number, fixer). Explain it once in the kickoff: the type tests pass only when the types are exact, and nobody edits types.check.ts.
  • Most common problems, and the nudge. fixer not optional (tsc on tickets.ts: "Property 'fixer' is missing"); the shown list or the count in useState (ask: can you work it out from the search and the switch?); the header as () => (...) (D2 fails: the field keeps only the first letter); numColumns without key={columns} (nothing fails at 390 wide; widen the web preview); markFixed editing the ticket in place (ticket.status = 'fixed': React does not re-render, D4 fails); a grouped heading without a background (the cards show through it when it is pinned).
  • Scoring. Run the four commands yourself on the hand-in (npm test, npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npx expo export --platform web --output-dir dist). Then a two-minute pass in the web preview at 390 and at 1024 wide, in light and dark mode (the browser's device toolbar and its rendering panel), with the search, both switches and one Mark fixed. Score each row from the evidence; write one sentence per row that is not "strong".
  • Pairs. Allowed if both can explain every line in the demo; score each learner's row 6 separately.
  • Resubmission. A row at 0 gets a written next step and one resubmission within two weeks. The Part 1 result is recorded when both the project and the assessment are met.

Part 1 Assessment

Taken in Session 9 after the project check-in: a written part (15 minutes, closed book, 10 points) and a practical (30 minutes, open book: lesson pages and their own code; no chat assistants, no classmates; 10 points). Total 20; 14 or more (70 %) = the Part 1 assessment met. Below that: one retake of the part that fell short, within two weeks.

Written part: questions, model answers, marking
W1
Metro bundles a file with a type error and the phone shows the app. Why does nothing complain, and which command finds the error? (1)
Metro removes the types and bundles the JavaScript that is left: it never checks them. npx tsc --noEmit (here npm run typecheck) reads the types and reports the error.
Marking: The point needs both halves: running is not checking, and a tsc command.
W2
A learner writes this line in the ticket card and npm run typecheck prints the error below. What does it mean, and how do you fix it? (2)
src/components/TicketCard.tsx:37:56 - error TS18048: 'ticket.fixer' is possibly 'undefined'.
Found 1 error in src/components/TicketCard.tsx:37
fixer is optional in Ticket (fixer?: string), so its type is string | undefined, and checking the status does not tell TypeScript that a fixer is there. Fix: check the property itself, ticket.fixer !== undefined && ... (or ticket.fixer?.toUpperCase()).
Marking: 1 point for "possibly undefined because it is optional", 1 for a fix that narrows. A non-null assertion ! or as string scores 0 for the fix.
W3
The café adds a fifth status, 'collected', to TicketStatus. What does npm run typecheck do next, and why is that useful? (1)
src/utils/tickets.ts:12:14 - error TS2741: Property 'collected' is missing in type '{ waiting: string; 'in-repair': string; fixed: string; 'not-fixable': string; }' but required in type 'Record<TicketStatus, string>'.
src/utils/tickets.ts:19:14 - error TS2741: Property 'collected' is missing in type '{ waiting: "neutral"; 'in-repair': "info"; fixed: "success"; 'not-fixable': "danger"; }' but required in type 'Record<TicketStatus, BadgeTone>'.
Found 2 errors in the same file, starting at: src/utils/tickets.ts:12
It reports every Record<TicketStatus, ...> table that has no entry for 'collected' (here statusLabels and statusTones, TS2741). The compiler lists every place the new status needs a decision before anything runs.
Marking: The point needs "it lists the tables missing the new key".
W4
On a phone, this card shows the text Fixer: and nothing else when there is no fixer, but a string straight inside a <View> stops the app. Which rule is behind the second, and which tool finds it? (1)
Every piece of text sits in a <Text> (AppText here); text straight in a View is an error when it runs (the red screen; in Jest Text strings must be rendered within a <Text> component). tsc does not find it: only running it (a test, the app).
Marking: The point needs the rule and "only running it".
W5
Why does the queue use keyExtractor={(ticket) => ticket.id} and not the index? (1)
A key tells the list which drawn row belongs to which ticket. When the search or Hide finished removes tickets, an index would point at a different ticket, so an open Show problem would jump to the wrong card. An id stays with its ticket.
Marking: Accept any answer that ties the key to the item's identity when the list changes.
W6
A teammate writes ListHeaderComponent={() => <SearchField ... />}. What does a volunteer notice on a phone, why, and what do you write instead? (2)
The keyboard closes after every letter (the field loses what is typed). A new function on every render is a new component type, so React throws the old header away and builds a new text field. Build the header as an element (const header = (...)) and pass that.
Marking: 1 point for the symptom and the reason, 1 for the element.
W7
The window gets wider than 700 and the queue goes from one column to two. Without key={columns} the screen stops. Why does the key fix it? (1)
A FlatList cannot change its number of columns (Changing numColumns on the fly is not supported). A new key tells React it is a different list, so it builds a new one with the new number of columns.
Marking: The point needs "a new key builds a new list".
W8
Name two things a phone's dark mode needs from the code, as the course does it. (1)
Any two of: colors by job in a light and a dark set (ThemeColors); styles made per theme (createThemedStyles), never a color baked in when the file loads; colors handed to props from useTheme(); a sticky heading with a background from the theme.
Marking: Half a point each, rounded down.

Recording results: Part 1 met

Part 1 met = the Fix-It Tables project complete under its rubric (no row at 0) AND the Part 1 assessment met: 14 or more of 20 points (70 %). A learner below either line gets the scoring sheet's "next step" in writing and one resubmission (project) or retake (assessment) within two weeks. When Part 1 runs as a course of its own, Part 1 met = the course complete; when the full course runs, it is a milestone (the course result is the final project and the written final).
